version: Original compatibility client 1.16.5.0; exact shutdown revision unverified

rules.finding: RequestCreateCharacterInSlot sends a seven-field tuple (slot, family, first, gender, height, appearance, race). Current server framing agrees.
Switches to characterselection(familyName, slotNum). Current server sends this before the changed pod CharacterInfo, matching the visible selection consumer.

rules.source: client/inputstate/characterselection.pyo OnDeleteCharacter line 114, offsets 37–55; client/ui/characterselectionwindow.pyo OnDeleteBtn line 335
rules.finding: Selection UI sends RequestDeleteCharacterInSlot with exactly one one-based slot in a tuple.

Require one-field tuple, checked integer-to-byte slot conversion and CharacterSelection session. Previously, 257 wrapped to 1; non-world states outside selection could also delete. Existing valid deletion and linked cleanup preserved.

rules.source: client/ui/charactercreationwindow.pyo _CreateCharacter line 694, offsets 195–216; Show line 232, offsets 467–508
rules.finding: Family text is always lower().capitalize() before sending; its editor is disabled while the account has characters. A persisted mixed-case family is therefore normalized even when the player cannot edit it.

The original UI sends Mcdonald for persisted McDonald. InternalCreate now matches the persisted family with OrdinalIgnoreCase and substitutes its existing spelling in the request before existing ownership/rename guards, so no family rename or new identity occurs. Success and pod replies retain McDonald. A genuinely different family remains refused while characters exist.

open_findings.finding: No direct creation/selection consumer connection established. Each audited SendCallUserMethod builds a tuple. Existing original-client log error occurs at startup before world admission; do not attribute it to creation packets without a native caller trace.

validation.tests: All 11 NewCharacterTests.Deletion cases pass in the full 1,246/1,246 rerun, including disconnected transport suppression with unchanged persistence checks.
validation.family_case_tests: Both normalized Mcdonald acceptance and Different refusal pass in the full 1,246/1,246 rerun, retaining persisted family spelling, cache/reply spelling, and account ownership.

first_combined_run.failure: Disconnected state test expected one failure reply, but transport intentionally drops outgoing packets. Character and appearance persistence assertions passed.
first_combined_run.correction: Test expects zero replies only for Disconnected; all other rejected states still require one. No production code change.

final_combined_run.scope: Full combined suite, including deletion states/wire framing, family normalization, first-login yaw migration Up/Down, and admission packet ordering. Source/workspace equality checked after completion; research docs updated separately.
